# Covarage Guides: Insurance Guides for Singapore SMEs

> Clear, sourced answers to the insurance questions Singapore business owners actually ask. Every fact links to a primary regulator, statute or named insurer document. Editorial firewall: no recommendations of specific insurers or policies. Covarage does not advise on, recommend, rank, compare or arrange insurance and, on request, introduces readers to a licensed insurance intermediary.

## Get it right (How-to guides)

- [Compulsory Motor Insurance in Singapore: What the Law Requires for Every Vehicle Your Business Runs](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/compulsory-motor-insurance-singapore-third-party): One of only two insurances Singapore law actually forces on a business. What the Motor Vehicles Act requires, for which vehicles, and what it does not.
- [Tenant vs Landlord: Who Insures What Under a Commercial Lease in Singapore](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/tenant-landlord-insurance-responsibilities-commercial-lease-singapore): No Singapore statute divides the insurance burden in a commercial lease. The covenants do, and they decide who insures the building and the fit-out.
- [How to Arrange Event Cancellation Insurance for a Singapore SME](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/event-cancellation-insurance-singapore-sme): Cancellation cover pays your own loss when the event cannot go ahead. Public liability pays someone else's. Assuming one covers the other is the costly error.
- [Business Interruption Sum Insured: The Gross-Profit Basis Explained](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/business-interruption-sum-insured-gross-profit-basis-singapore): Singapore insurers rate business interruption on insurable gross profit, not the figure in your accounts. It is turnover minus only the variable costs.
- [Commercial Property and Fire Insurance for Singapore SMEs: The Complete Guide](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/commercial-property-fire-complete-guide-singapore): No statute forces you to insure your own premises. Your lease and your lender almost certainly do, and their wording decides the sum insured you need.
- [Foreign Worker Insurance in Singapore: WICA, Medical, and Repatriation, End to End](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/foreign-worker-insurance-complete-guide-singapore): Hiring a Work Permit or S Pass holder is not one insurance decision. Several duties start at once under EFMA, and they attach at different moments.
- [Construction Insurance in Singapore: BCA, SCAL, CAR and the Full Picture](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/construction-insurance-complete-guide-singapore): Construction insurance is a stack of separate covers, not one policy. Only work injury compensation is mandated by statute; the rest arrives by contract.
- [Professional Indemnity Insurance for Singapore Service Businesses: The Complete Guide](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/professional-indemnity-complete-guide-singapore): No Singapore law makes professional indemnity universal. It is compulsory for named regulated professions and demanded by contract for everyone else.
- [Cyber Insurance for Singapore SMEs: The Complete Guide](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/cyber-insurance-complete-guide-singapore-sme): No statute requires cyber insurance. What is mandatory are the PDPA duties that create the exposure, and that is where the real obligation sits.
- [Public Liability Insurance for Singapore SMEs: The Complete Guide](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/public-liability-complete-guide-singapore-sme): What public liability pays when your premises or your operations injure someone or damage their property, and where the cover stops short.
- [WICA: The Complete Guide to Work Injury Compensation for Singapore Employers](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/wica-complete-guide-singapore-employers): Singapore's WICA makes an employer liable regardless of fault and creates two separate duties. Which employees must be insured, and what the Act compels.
- [Trade Credit Insurance for Singapore SMEs: How It Actually Works](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/trade-credit-insurance-how-it-works-singapore): Trade credit insurance responds when an insured buyer fails to pay or goes insolvent. What it covers, what it excludes, and what it asks of you.
- [Contribution Between Insurers: When Multiple Policies Cover the Same Loss](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/contribution-between-insurers-singapore): When two policies cover the same loss, contribution decides how the Singapore insurers share it. Why double cover has never meant double payment.
- [Subrogation: When Your Insurer Recovers from a Third Party](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/subrogation-insurer-recovery-singapore): After paying you, a Singapore insurer steps into your rights and pursues whoever caused the loss. What subrogation asks of you, and what can forfeit it.
- [The Average Clause Explained: Singapore Underinsurance Penalties on Partial Losses](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/average-clause-underinsurance-singapore): If the sum insured is below the true value, the average clause cuts every partial claim in proportion. How underinsurance quietly reduces what you get paid.
- [Sub-limits, Aggregates, and Deductibles: How Singapore Commercial Insurance Policies Actually Pay](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/sub-limits-aggregates-deductibles-singapore): The headline sum insured is only the first of four limits. Sub-limits, aggregates and deductibles decide what actually reaches your bank account.
- [How to Read a Singapore Commercial Insurance Policy: The Six Sections That Matter Most](https://covarage.com/guides/document-legal/reading-commercial-insurance-policy-singapore): A commercial policy runs 30 to 60 pages around six core sections. Which sections decide whether it responds, and the order to read them in.
- [How to Request and Read Your Claims Experience Report: A Singapore SME's Practical Guide](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/claims-experience-report-singapore-sme): The claims experience report is the most material document at a Singapore renewal. What it records, what it reveals, and how to read it before the insurer.
- [How to File a Data Breach Notification Under PDPA Part 6A: The PDPC 3-Day Clock](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/pdpa-data-breach-notification-3-day-pdpc-singapore): Singapore's PDPA Part 6A gives three calendar days to notify PDPC once a breach is notifiable. What starts the clock, and what the notice must carry.
- [How to File a Workplace Accident Notification Under WICA 2019: The 10-Day MOM Rule](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/wica-workplace-accident-notification-10-day-mom-singapore): Singapore's WICA requires an employer to notify MOM of a work accident within ten days. What counts as reportable, when the clock starts, what to file.
- [How to Prepare Information So Your Insurance Claim Gets Processed Faster](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/insurance-claim-preparation-singapore): Two things slow most Singapore commercial claims: a notification that misses its deadline or format, and missing documents. What to have ready first.
- [How to Brief Your Insurance Adviser So Quotes Come Back Faster and More Accurate](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/how-to-brief-insurance-adviser-singapore): Quotes come back wrong because briefs go out incomplete. The five errors that cause it in Singapore, starting with payroll estimated rather than counted.
- [How to Build an Insurance Renewal Process That Survives Staff Turnover](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/insurance-renewal-process-staff-turnover-singapore): Most Singapore SMEs run insurance off one person's memory. What happens at renewal when that person leaves, and how to make the calendar survive them.
- [The 12 Insurance Dates Every Singapore SME Must Track](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/12-insurance-renewal-dates-singapore-sme): A typical SME insurance programme has twelve recurring dates. What each one is, and the specific consequence of missing it.
- [The Hidden Cost of a Missed Insurance Renewal for Singapore Businesses](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/missed-insurance-renewal-cost-singapore-sme): A Singapore commercial policy lapses at expiry, or at day 60 unpaid. There is no grace period, and this is what a lapse actually costs.
- [The Document Trail That Saved (and the Missing Document That Sank) a Singapore Business Insurance Claim](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/document-trail-business-insurance-claim-singapore): Claims are rarely lost in dispute. They are lost in documentation. The three things a Singapore insurer needs proved, and the papers that prove them.

What to gather first, and what to look for.
- [Why Email and WhatsApp Are the Worst Places to Store Business Insurance Policies](https://covarage.com/guides/procedural-howto/email-whatsapp-business-insurance-storage-singapore): Insurance documents stored in personal email and WhatsApp fail exactly when needed.
